## Goal
`check_scheduler` (`doctor.py:247-266`) turns `scheduler.status()` text into a result by looking only for "not supported" and "not installed"; anything else is `ok`. But `status()` (`scheduler/__init__.py:183-210`) also returns "systemd timer: inactive, disabled" (installed but not running), "launchd agent installed, not loaded" and "cron job installed". The first two are reported as OK although no check will ever run, so a person who thinks they are protected is not. Classify the exact strings `status()` produces: systemd needs `active` and `enabled`; launchd needs "loaded"; "scheduled task installed" and "cron job installed" are ok. A not-running case becomes `warn` with the fix "Run `freemyid schedule install` again." The strings are matched by a small table built from the module's own constants so a wording change in `scheduler` fails a test instead of silently passing. `doctor/1` JSON keys and ids stay the same.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Table over the exact `status()` outputs: "systemd timer: active, enabled" -> ok; "systemd timer: inactive, disabled" -> warn; "systemd timer: active, disabled" -> warn; "systemd timer: unknown, unknown" -> warn; "cron job installed" -> ok; "launchd agent loaded" -> ok; "launchd agent installed, not loaded" -> warn; "scheduled task installed" -> ok; "not installed" -> warn (existing text kept); "Scheduling is not supported on this system." -> warn (existing text kept).
2. An unrecognised string is `ok` with the detail shown as before (never a new failure), so a future wording does not turn doctor red.
3. A scheduler exception still gives the existing warn (`doctor.py:252-255`).
4. The `fix` strings of the existing branches are unchanged; the new warn has a plain-words fix with no shell-only syntax on Windows (no `$USER`).
5. `doctor/1` doc, check ids and order are unchanged; counts change only for the new warn cases.
6. WO-260/283/405 tests and existing doctor tests pass unchanged.

This is Codex code-lane work (owner, 2026-11-09): fix and improve the listed module(s) directly, with tests; don't xfail a bug you can fix here. No contract changes: public function signatures, `src/freemyid/models.py`, `interfaces.py`, schema files, `--json` shapes and documented CLI output stay as they are (additive helpers inside the listed files are fine). If the work turns out to need a contract change, stop and say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md "Questions for the owner". Fake data only, offline (fake fetchers, no network), Windows-safe paths in tests (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`, no `/tmp`). Typed, ruff-clean, small diff. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing (2026-11-09); re-check them.
